title: Sudan Civil War Tracker Update — Thu May 28, 2026
summary: RSF fighters and allied Arab militias massacred between 28 and 97 Masalit civilians in Misterei, West Darfur on May 28 — burning the town to the ground in a coordinated ground assault involving motorcycles, horses, and armed pickup trucks. Satellite fire detection confirmed the destruction across all residential areas. The attack is among at least seven West Darfur towns burned by RSF since April 2026, continuing the pattern of ethnically targeted atrocities against Masalit and non-Arab communities. SAF continued drone strikes targeting RSF positions in North Kordofan as the multi-front military campaign proceeds. The attack occurred one week after the Treaty of Jeddah humanitarian framework was signed, demonstrating ongoing RSF atrocities in Darfur despite diplomatic instruments.

title: Sudan Civil War Tracker Update — Wed May 27, 2026
summary: RSF drones struck Al-Tina market on the Sudan-Chad border on May 25, killing 14 civilians and prompting Chad to close its Sudan frontier — threatening the primary refugee and humanitarian corridor into Darfur. On the same day, RSF drones targeted RAC leader Musa Hilal's compound in Mustariha, North Darfur, killing several commanders while Hilal survived. A fast-spreading cholera outbreak was reported in Khartoum (2,500 cases in three weeks; 633 cases and 24 deaths May 23 alone), with over 1 million children at risk. On Eid al-Adha, Gen. Burhan announced plans for a comprehensive post-RSF political dialogue to formulate Sudan's new governance structure, explicitly excluding the RSF. SAF drone strikes continued on RSF positions in North Kordofan.

title: Sudan Civil War Tracker Update — Sun May 24, 2026

On May 23, SAF captured Dibebad, the strategic 'Tayba Triangle' crossroads in South Kordofan, tightening the cordon on RSF-SPLM-N logistics; IOM documented 565 households displaced. A SAF airstrike on an RSF-SPLM-N supply convoy near Yabus, Blue Nile State killed 5 and injured 20, continuing SAF's aerial interdiction of the Kurmuk–Damazin axis. Map-lines and map-points updated for all new strike and capture events.

title: Sudan Civil War Tracker Update — Fri May 22, 2026
summary: SAF declared White Nile State fully cleared of RSF presence, securing the supply corridor to the Kordofan and Blue Nile fronts as SAF's multi-front offensive consolidates territorial gains. A May 19 drone strike on a crowded market in Ghubaysh, West Kordofan, killed at least 28 civilians — among the deadliest single strikes of the month — with witnesses describing a two-stage attack. The civilian toll from drone warfare continues to mount as the June–August lean season approaches with 19.5 million facing acute food insecurity and the humanitarian appeal only ~20% funded.

title: Sudan Civil War Tracker Update — Thu May 21, 2026
summary: SAF and RSF signed the Treaty of Jeddah on May 20, committing both warring parties to civilian protection and humanitarian access — the first formal humanitarian framework signed by both sides in the conflict. The agreement arrived as SAF broke the Dilling siege for a third time, recapturing Al-Takma in South Kordofan and reopening the Dilling–Kadugli road; the first supply convoy in four months reached famine-confirmed Kadugli, collapsing food prices from SDG 40,000 to SDG 13,000/kg. Sudan's Security and Defence Council formally commended SAF gains across South Kordofan, Blue Nile, and Darfur. UN Human Rights Chief Türk's high-alert from May 11 documented 880+ civilian drone deaths in January–April 2026 — over 80% of all conflict deaths — underscoring the Treaty's challenge. New event files created for May 20–21; map-lines and map-points updated for the Dilling siege break and Kadugli humanitarian corridor; KPIs, political, and claims sections updated.

SAF drone strikes on Nyala extended to a fifth consecutive day; the RSF cut all telecommunications in the city to suppress documentation. Three new map entries added: the Day 5 Nyala strike line, the Wadi al-Atrun SAF advance line, and the Wadi al-Atrun map point. Political section updated with Malik Agar's formal TSC appointment.

SAF extended its aerial campaign against RSF positions in Nyala to a fourth consecutive day (May 15–18), targeting Al-Masane weapons depots while Hemedti reportedly remains in the city. title: Sudan Civil War Tracker Update — Thu May 14, 2026
summary: On Day 1125, the SAF-aligned government formally returned to Khartoum from Port Sudan — ending a 25-month wartime displacement — with the Central Bank resuming capital operations for the first time since April 2023. SAF airstrikes on Al Zorg — Hemedti's North Darfur hometown — killed at least 64 civilians, destroyed the local hospital, and killed two of Hemedti's relatives, in one of the war's most symbolically charged strikes. Map-points and map-lines updated with the Al Zorg strike; political section updated to reflect Hemedti's brother's EU sanctions and the strikes on his hometown.

title: Sudan Civil War Tracker Update — Wed May 13, 2026
summary: On Day 1124, SAF conducted coordinated dual-front advances: retaking Al-Hamadi in South Kordofan (Hawazma administrative hub) and clearing the Al-Jami'a and Al-Shaqla neighborhoods in southern Omdurman, eliminating the last significant RSF pockets in the greater Khartoum metro area. New IPC analysis released this week confirms Sudan has become the world's hungriest country, with famine confirmed in El Fasher and Kadugli, risk extending to two new Darfur areas, and 19.1 million people at IPC3+ acute food insecurity. On May 12, SAF drones struck four simultaneous targets in Al-Daein, East Darfur, including RSF commanders' residences and the Andour Well civilian water source. Asharq Al-Awsat analysts assess that three senior RSF defections in two months — including Brig. Gen. El Safana's May 11 departure — may mark the beginning of an RSF 'breakup phase.' Khartoum airport entered a fourth day of closure while Sudan's Prime Minister visited the site; the UN and UK formally condemned the RSF drone strikes. An Al Jazeera analysis published May 8 projected Sudan's prolonged war could cost $34.5 billion in GDP losses and push 34 million more people into extreme poverty by 2030. New map points added for Gedaref and East Gallabat border zone; SAF border deployment line added to map. title: Sudan Civil War Tracker Update — Thu May 7, 2026

An RSF drone strike on May 5 killed 5 civilians at two fuel stations in Kosti, White Nile State — added to the map and events. The Kenana agro-industrial complex economic impact has been added to the economic tracker. Sudan's civil war now at Day 1118 with approximately 34 million people requiring urgent humanitarian aid.

title: Sudan Civil War Tracker Update — Wed May 6, 2026

SAF air defenses intercepted the May 5 drone before it reached the airport; Khartoum International Airport was closed for 72 hours. On May 6, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, the US, and EU condemned the attacks without endorsing Sudan's specific accusations, while both the UAE and Ethiopia denied any involvement. New events, a new map-line showing the drone trajectory from Bahir Dar to Khartoum airport, and a new contested claim and political figure have been added.

title: Sudan Conflict Update — Apr 20, 2026

Al Jazeera published a field report from Sudan's only functioning tropical diseases hospital in Omdurman, documenting the collapse of the country's healthcare system: WHO data now records 2,052 people killed in 217+ attacks on health facilities since April 2023, with 37% of Sudan's facilities non-functional. KPI and casualty data updated to reflect the latest WHO healthcare toll figures.

title: Sudan Conflict Update — Apr 9, 2026

An African Union assessment delegation led by Special Envoy Belaiche concluded its Khartoum visit recommending the AU resume office operations in the capital — the first AU assessment mission to Khartoum since the AU evacuated at war's outbreak in April 2023. Military sources disclosed 850+ foreign mercenaries embedded with the RSF including Colombian 'Desert Wolves' drone specialists and Russian technical advisors transited through Somalia and Libya, highlighting the conflict's deepening internationalization and the Colombian specialists' contribution to RSF drone warfare against SAF-held towns.

title: Sudan Conflict Update — Apr 8, 2026
summary: SAF drone strike on April 8 killed Hamid Ali Abubakar — commander-in-chief of the RSF-aligned Sudanese Awakening Revolutionary Council (RAC) and a security adviser to Hemedti — at a command meeting in Damrat al-Firdous, Central Darfur, marking one of the highest-value SAF targeted kills in the Darfur theater. SAF simultaneously secured Al-Tukma (7km east of Dilling, South Kordofan) and fully reopened the Dilling–North Kordofan supply road, breaking the RSF-SPLM-N partial siege of the city following weeks of artillery bombardment of residential areas. A concurrent RSF assault on Al-Tumat neighborhood west of Dilling was repelled. International mediators confirmed Berlin Conference preparatory talks for Addis Ababa on April 10–12, ahead of the April 15 ministerial conference, though ongoing boycott threats from multiple Sudanese political factions cloud the process.
